children: Veteran trader Peter Brandt said late Saturday that Bitcoin’s (BTC) record high set last year may never be surpassed in his lifetime if a bearish head-and-shoulders (H&S) pattern on the cryptocurrency’s weekly chart holds.

Brandt posted the chart on X and asked whether it showed a “legit H&S top.” If it was, he said, he could build a technical case that Bitcoin’s all-time high (ATH) was already behind it. “The ATH is in, not to be surpassed at least in my lifetime,” he wrote.

A head-and-shoulders top has three peaks, with the middle one the highest. Traders often read it as a sign that a rally is ending. Brandt’s chart showed Bitcoin at $62,830, down about 16% for the week and trading roughly 50% below its record of over $126,000 set in October last year.

Brandt returned to the pattern, posting a linear-scale version of the chart, which put the pattern’s measured downside target at negative $10,487. “On a linear scale the downside target is a big minus number,” he wrote, adding that logarithmic scale “must be used” to work out the target.
Thorne Sees A Bullish Bottom

Not everyone, however, read that chart as a top. James Thorne, chief market strategist at Wellington-Altus, saw a bullish inverse head-and-shoulders instead. According to Thorne, the pattern was “intact,” with a left shoulder at $59,000, a head at $57,000, and a right shoulder “forming now.”

Thorne said Bitcoin needed to reclaim $73,000 and confirm a move above $87,000. From there, he targeted $117,000 by mid-2027, then a break of the record and $150,000 to $170,000 by the end of that year. “This washout was leverage, not fundamentals. Buy the fear,” he wrote. Below $57,000, he said, he would be wrong.
ETF Outflows Keep Mounting

Selling has also shown up in U.S. spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs), as SoSoValue data showed that investors pulled about $2.35 billion from the funds over the two weeks through Friday, marking one of the largest two-week outflows, according to data from Coinglass.
BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) led the outflows, logging eleven straight sessions of outflows, which accounted for roughly 90% of November's total spot Bitcoin ETF outflows.
